full_story_part1.text: It was a small twist. Behind a service that lets people ask AI to make phone calls, humans were actually making the calls. That kind of test was being carried out. The main player was Muse, Meta's AI assistant. Muse can call businesses and stores in the United States to book haircuts, check whether items are in stock, and get price estimates from businesses. If AI can take care of troublesome phone calls, it seems very useful. However, in some tests of its calling feature, trained human contract workers made the calls instead of AI. They handled the conversations all the way to the end. The issue was not that humans made the calls themselves. The issue was how to tell users who was speaking.

full_story_part1.canonical_text:
It was a small twist. Behind a service that lets people ask AI to make phone calls, humans were actually making the calls. That kind of test was being carried out.

The main player was Muse, Meta’s AI assistant. Muse can call businesses and stores in the United States to book haircuts, check whether items are in stock, and get price estimates from businesses. If AI can take care of troublesome phone calls, it seems very useful.

However, in some tests of its calling feature, trained human contract workers made the calls instead of AI. They handled the conversations all the way to the end.

The issue was not that humans made the calls themselves. The issue was how to tell users who was speaking.

full_story_part2.text: People who asked Muse to make a call might think that AI was making it. But in some cases, a human was speaking. And if this was not properly explained, users had no way to know whether they were talking to AI or a person. They were enjoying the convenience of AI, only to find a human on the other end of the call without realizing it. That was what was happening behind the scenes. Also, when user information was needed to continue a call, it might be shared unintentionally with contract workers at a call center. Meta employees pointed this out internally as a privacy concern.

full_story_part3.text: News reports also cited an employee's report that human staff made inappropriate comments about race during calls to negotiate internet or cable fees. However, this is one report. It would be wrong to apply it to all contract workers. A Meta executive admitted that starting the test without properly explaining it was a mistake. The company also restored the human concierge feature to the way it had been before, at least for now. The real challenge for AI phone calls is not just how they talk. It is whether they can honestly tell people who is on the other end of the call. The more useful a service is, the less it should hide the people working behind the scenes. The Muse case showed us this simple but important point.
